questions.markdown:
Consider a Markov chain with state space $S=\{0,1\}$, where 0 represents rain and 1 represents no rain; $X_n$ - weather on day $n$. We assume that:

- If it rains today, then it will rain tomorrow with probability $0.75$,
- If it does not rain today, then it will rain tomorrow with probability $0.35$

What is the probability that it will rain four days from today given that it is raining today?

The factory has 2 machines and one repair crew. Assume that probability of any one machine breaking down on a given day is $\alpha$. Assume that if the repair crew is working on a machine, the probability that it will complete the repair in a day is $\beta$. For simplicity, ignore the probability of repair completion or breakdown taking place except at the end of the day. Let $X_n$ be the number of machines in operation at the end of the $n^{\text{th}}$ day. Assume the behavior of $X_n$ can be modeled as a Markov chain.

Write Transition probability matrix for above defined problem.

For sufficiently small $h>0$, prove the following property of the Poisson process $\{X(t): t\geq 0\}$ with state space $S=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$,

$$
p_{i,j}(h)=P(X(t+h)=j\mid X(t)=i)=o(h),\; j\geq i+2
$$

where $o(h)$ is the order of '$h$' and satisfies $\lim_{h\to 0}\dfrac{o(h)}{h}=0$, $\lambda$ is the rate of occurrence of events.

Prove that the steady state solution of $M/M/1$ queueing model yields

$$
p_n=\left(\frac{\lambda}{\mu}\right)^n p_0,
$$

where $p_n$ is the probability of having '$n$' customers, $p_0$ denotes the probability of having '0' customers in the system, $\lambda$ is arrival rate of the customers and $\mu$ is service rate of the servers in the system.

A Commercial bank has 3 cash paying assistants customers are found to arrive in a Poisson fashion at an average rate of $6$/hr for business transaction. The service time is found to have an E.D with a mean of 18 mins. The customers are processed on FCFS basis. Calculate average number of customers in the system.

Let $X=\{X_1,X_2\}$ and $Y=\{Y_1,Y_2\}$ be two groups of variables and $Z=(X,Y)^T$. The Covariance matrix of $Z$ is given below.

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
4.0 & 2.1 & 0.3 & 1.2\\
2.1 & 3.5 & 0.4 & 0.9\\
0.3 & 0.4 & 2.0 & 0.5\\
1.2 & 0.9 & 0.5 & 3.1
\end{bmatrix}
$$

a. Find the Covariance of $(X_1,Y_2)$.

b. Find the Variance of $Y_1$.

Provided the data of 10 number of observations with its mean vector as

$$
\bar{X}=\begin{pmatrix}4097.5\\1468.2\\3700.1\end{pmatrix}
$$

and variance-covariance matrix as

$$
S=\begin{pmatrix}
12497245 & 3634519 & 11454489\\
3634519 & 1265551 & 3317404\\
11454489 & 3317404 & 10817991
\end{pmatrix},
$$

the $T^2$ statistic calculated as $26.56274$.

Test the hypothesis

$$
H_0:\begin{bmatrix}\mu_1\\\mu_2\\\mu_3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2000\\1200\\2500\end{bmatrix}
\;\text{vs}\;
H_1:\begin{bmatrix}\mu_1\\\mu_2\\\mu_3\end{bmatrix}\ne\begin{bmatrix}2000\\1200\\2500\end{bmatrix}
$$

Calculate $\mathrm{SST}_r$, $\mathrm{SSR}$ and $\mathrm{SSE}$ for the following data

| $X_1$ | $X_2$ | $Y$ |
|---|---:|---:|
| 15 | 30 | 4 |
| 12 | 24 | 6 |
| 8  | 20 | 7 |
| 6  | 14 | 9 |
| 4  | 10 | 13 |
| 3  | 4  | 15 |

With the given regression equation as

$$
\hat{Y}=16.48+0.39\,X_1-0.62\,X_2.
$$

questions.markdown:
Consider a one-way MANOVA study with 4 groups and 2 dependent variables. The sum of squares and cross-products matrices are:

- Between-group matrix $(B)$:

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
36 & 12\\
12 & 48
\end{pmatrix}
$$

- Within-group matrix $(W)$:

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
90 & 30\\
30 & 100
\end{pmatrix}
$$

Calculate Wilks' Lambda statistic.

The following observations on two responses are collected for three treatments. The observation vectors $\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\x_2\end{bmatrix}$ are

Treatment 1: $\begin{bmatrix}4\\6\end{bmatrix}$, $\begin{bmatrix}3\\7\end{bmatrix}$, $\begin{bmatrix}7\\5\end{bmatrix}$, $\begin{bmatrix}5\\8\end{bmatrix}$, $\begin{bmatrix}4\\8\end{bmatrix}$,

Treatment 2: $\begin{bmatrix}4\\5\end{bmatrix}$, $\begin{bmatrix}2\\7\end{bmatrix}$, $\begin{bmatrix}2\\5\end{bmatrix}$,

Treatment 3: $\begin{bmatrix}3\\6\end{bmatrix}$, $\begin{bmatrix}6\\2\end{bmatrix}$, $\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix}$, $\begin{bmatrix}3\\4\end{bmatrix}$.

Construct the one-way MANOVA Table.

The following data set is obtained from a study conducted to determine the effect of job stress on work safety perception. Two measurements $(p=2)$, job stress and safety perception were taken on two groups of people with sample size of 19. The mean vectors and covariance matrices are as follows:

For group-1:

$$
\bar{X}=\begin{bmatrix}140\\420\end{bmatrix};\quad S=\begin{pmatrix}550 & 210\\210 & 330\end{pmatrix},
$$

For group-2:

$$
\bar{X}=\begin{bmatrix}150\\400\end{bmatrix};\quad S=\begin{pmatrix}480 & 250\\250 & 530\end{pmatrix},
$$

The management claims that there is no significant difference in job stress and safety perception between the two groups of employees. Does the data substantiate the claim at $\alpha=0.01$?
Consider a set of 5 one-dimensional data points 50, 51, 55, 57, 60. Apply Agglomerative clustering algorithm to build the hierarchical clustering dendogram. Merge the clusters using MIN distance.

Compute the linear discriminant projection of the following two-dimensional dataset:

- Class $C_1$: $(4,1)$, $(2,4)$, $(2,3)$, $(3,6)$
- Class $C_2$: $(9,10)$, $(6,8)$, $(9,5)$, $(8,7)$

Given the data in the table, reduce the dimension from 2 to 1 using the principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm.

| $X_1$ | 2 | 0 | 3 | 1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $X_2$ | 0 | 1 | 1 | 2 |
